purpose: Source register for skeleton-first canonical proportion work. Values are evidence inputs, not hard production targets.
policy: Use multiple independent sources; preserve population/method context; do not scale a single-study mean directly into the character without cross-checking.

sources.note: Already integrity-checked in proportion_report.json; direct bony forearm regression still to be computed reproducibly from the committed CSV.

sources.citation: Beredjiklian PK et al. Correlation between Adult Height and Metacarpal Length Using Advanced Imaging Modalities. Arch Bone Jt Surg. 2025;13(6):345-348.
sources.population: 40 skeletally mature adults; 28 men, 12 women; mean height 175.3 cm
use: cross-check hand ray ordering and scale
sources.limitation: Mixed-sex small sample; thumb value not in accessible abstract; do not stature-scale as a sole target.

sources.citation: Mathematical relations between the lengths of the metacarpal bones and phalanges: surgical significance.
sources.limitation: Single regional sample and 2D radiographs; use with the independent 2025 CT means and the character's stature-conditioned ANSUR hand-length corridor before freezing targets.
sources.measurement_definition: Head and base limits of each metacarpal/phalanx; midpoint-to-midpoint proximodistal length on standardized AP hand radiographs.

reported_relations.metacarpals: M1 = 0.67*M2 = 0.71*M3 = 0.78*M4 = 0.84*M5 (paper notation expresses equivalent pairwise ratios; Table 1 should be used for exact pairwise conversion).
reported_relations.note: Use the descriptive male means/SDs above for the first canonical corridor; pairwise ratios are a secondary shape check.

sources.citation: Hoang D et al. An Anatomical Study of Metacarpal Morphology Utilizing CT Scans. J Hand Surg Am. 2021.
sources.limitation: Accessible abstract does not expose numerical per-ray lengths.

sources.citation: Evaluation of metatarsal relationships in the biomechanics of 332 normal feet using the method of measuring relative lengths.
sources.normal_pattern: Index-minus most frequent; all three metatarsal formulas can be normal.
sources.limitation: Radiographic relative-length method is not identical to osteometric bone length; use ratios/patterns before absolute values.

sources.citation: Dogan A et al. Morphometric study of the human metatarsals and phalanges. Clin Anat. 2007;20(2):209-214.
use: metatarsal and toe phalanx internal proportions
sources.limitation: Accessible abstract confirms fixed proportions but does not expose the numerical formulas; full table/formulas required before final target.

sources.citation: Measurement of three-dimensional morphological characteristics of the calcaneus using CT image post-processing.
use: calcaneus length/height geometry and sex/height adjustment
sources.limitation: Accessible abstract confirms measured parameters and height-adjusted sex analysis but not numerical values.

sources.citation: Hind- and midfoot bone morphology varies with foot type and sex.
use: shape variability bounds for calcaneus, talus, navicular, cuboid
sources.limitation: Useful for variability/shape classes, not a single canonical length.
Model-specific generic geometries; never used as the sole anatomical truth.

sources.limitation: Accessible abstract confirms regressions but does not expose coefficients or means; full table required before setting a numeric canonical target.

sources.citation: Torimitsu S et al. Stature estimation based on radial and ulnar lengths using three-dimensional images from multidetector computed tomography in a Japanese population. Leg Med. 2014.
sources.limitation: Population-specific; accessible abstract gives SEE but not coefficients/mean lengths.

sources.citation: Gul H et al. Estimation of Body Stature Using the Percutaneous Length of Ulna of an Individual. Cureus. 2020.
sources.limitation: Percutaneous ulna definition is not dry-bone maximum length and population-specific; use only as a cross-check, never as the primary skeletal target.

sources.citation: Meadows L, Jantz RL. Allometric secular change in the long bones from the 1800s to the present. J Forensic Sci. 1995.
use: guard against constant-ratio scaling of long bones

sources.limitation: Historical US male samples; informs scaling policy, not a target length.

sources.citation: Malone PSC et al. Anatomic Relationships of the Distal and Proximal Radioulnar Joints Articulating Surface Areas and of the Radius and Ulna Bone Volumes. Front Bioeng Biotechnol. 2016.

sources.citation: Barrôco R et al. Evaluation of metatarsal relationships in the biomechanics of 332 normal feet using the method of measuring relative lengths. Rev Bras Ortop. 2011/2015.
sources.population: 166 adults aged 25-50; 83 men and 83 women; 332 normal weight-bearing feet
sources.normal_pattern: Index-minus most frequent; M1 about 2.4 mm shorter than M2, M3 4.4 mm shorter than M2, M4 9.2 mm shorter than M3, M5 14.7 mm shorter than M4.
use: forefoot ray ordering and relative pattern under weight bearing
sources.limitation: Measurements are relative distances from a Chopart reference line to metatarsal heads, not osteometric metatarsal bone lengths.

sources.citation: Kwon BK et al. Morphologic evaluation of cervical spine anatomy with computed tomography: anterior cervical plate fixation considerations. J Spinal Disord Tech. 2004.
sources.population: CT studies from 50 males and 50 females
sources.limitation: Primarily body width/depth, not inter-level centre positions or disc-centre spacing.

sources.citation: Disc and Vertebral Body Morphology From Birth to Adulthood. Spine. 2022.
use: adult vertebral body/disc height plausibility and regional trend
sources.limitation: Growth-study endpoint values are regional summaries, not per-level adult male canonical coordinates.

sources.citation: Cross-sectional properties of rib geometry from an adult population. Front Bioeng Biotechnol. 2023.
use: population-derived rib cross-sectional geometry by rib number and normalized rib position
sources.limitation: Cross-section geometry does not by itself provide the full curved rib centreline or costovertebral axis.
sources.bibliographic_alias_guard: Shared PMID/DOI with another legacy record in canonical_source_identity_review_v1.json; count once as a publication. Distinct publication identities still require independent-cohort review.

sources.citation: Patil S et al. Radiological Biometric Study of Metatarsals and Phalanges. J Clin Diagn Res. 2017;11(9):AC05-AC09.

use: confirm whether a003 long foot is skeletal as well as surface
sources.limitation: Single regional sample and 2D radiographs. Distal phalanx comparison to a003 is weaker because the current armature distal tip can include a surface-tip allowance.

sources.citation: Patterson RM et al. Carpal bone anatomy measured by computer analysis of three-dimensional reconstructions of computed tomography images. J Hand Surg Am. 1995.

use: relative 3D spacing independent of surface mesh

sources.citation: Three-dimensional carpal alignment: computer-aided CT analysis of carpal axes and normal ranges. J Hand Surg Eur Vol. 2023.
sources.limitation: Angles depend on the study's radial coordinate system; must map frames explicitly before applying.

sources.citation: Postero-anterior radiography of the wrist. Normal database of carpal measurements. Surg Radiol Anat. 1998.

sources.citation: Mahakkanukrauh P et al. Sex estimation from upper limb bones in a Thai population. Anat Cell Biol. 2020;53(1):36-43.

measurement_definitions.max_humerus: Most superior point on humeral head to most inferior point on trochlea.
measurement_definitions.max_ulna: Most superior point on olecranon to most inferior point on styloid.
measurement_definitions.physiological_ulna: Most distal point on coronoid-process surface to most distal point on inferior surface of distal ulnar head.
measurement_definitions.max_radius: Most proximally positioned point on radial head to styloid tip, without regard for long axis.

use: maximum ulna/humerus plausibility after endpoint conversion
sources.limitation: Population-specific direct osteometry. Current a003 ulna maximum requires an estimated olecranon allowance, so radius is the cleaner comparison.

sources.citation: Forensic Anthropology reference text/table: male Aboriginal left radius and ulna dimensions.
sources.limitation: Reference-table source rather than the primary measurement publication; left side only. Use as corroboration, not the sole target.

sources.citation: Pretorius HS, Ferreira N, Burger MC. A computer tomography-based anthropomorphic study of forearm osteology: implications for prosthetic design. SA Orthop J. 2021;20(3).

measurement_definition.radius: overall length from midpoint of wrist to centre of radial head
measurement_definition.ulna: overall length from midpoint of olecranon to centre of distal ulna

use: measurement-defined adult CT cross-check for radius/ulna segment geometry
distal radius soft/landmark conversion sanity check
sources.limitation: Predominantly male but not male-only; mean stature not reported; radius endpoint is wrist midpoint rather than radial styloid and ulna endpoint is olecranon midpoint rather than maximum olecranon tip.

sources.citation: Rausch V et al. The radial head size in relation to osseous landmarks of the forearm. Surg Radiol Anat. 2019.

sources.limitation: Mixed-sex cadaver sample; accessible abstract does not fully expose endpoint definitions, so it cannot freeze canonical length.
sources.measurement_definition: Radius: styloid tip to radial-head articular surface. Ulna: styloid tip to coronoid base (not olecranon), so it is not whole-ulna length. 41 embalmed specimens, 19 male and 22 female. Published 2019 (Surg Radiol Anat 41(4)).

sources.limitation: Cadaveric Chinese sample; talus length definition is study-specific and not the same as the current HGPT talus control-stick span.
sources.measurement_caution: Values describe the superior talar dome study definitions, not whole-talus maximum length (male whole talus 53-58 mm in dry-bone studies). Do not use as whole-bone scale.

sources.citation: Morphometric Analysis of the Calcaneus in a Southeast Asian Population. 2024.

sources.citation: Holcombe SA, Wang SC, Grotberg JB. The effect of age and demographics on rib shape. J Anat. 2017.

weight strongly associated with pump-handle angle
